# Grids and geometry {#sec-ch03}

<!-- PROVENANCE
pin: snapy@919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274 (chengcli/snapy, code_pin.yml)
sources: OUTLINE.md, grids and geometry; book map draft 2 (mechanism homes); the code at the pin
status: draft
-->

This chapter describes the grids snapy integrates on and what a ghost cell holds. It covers the three working
coordinate systems (Cartesian, spherical-polar and the gnomonic equiangular cubed sphere) with the metric
quantities the finite-volume update uses: face areas, cell volumes, centroids, widths, geometric source terms and
the local frames of the Riemann problems. It also covers the curved-grid helpers that the face-flux corrections of
@sec-ch04 read, how the one global grid is cut into blocks and ranks, and what each kind of ghost contains at a
physical face, an internal face, a cubed-sphere panel edge and an $x_1$[^rg-65581851d3d4] seam between blocks. How ghost values are
carried (buffers, tags, backends) is the subject of @sec-ch14; here only what they are is described. All code is
cited at the pin of `code_pin.yml`. The schemes are listed in @tbl-ch03-schemes; their switch couplings are in the switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.

Which grid to choose for a domain, with each grid's requirements, added work per stage and limits, is answered at
@sec-ch03-choosing, at the end of the chapter. How the three grids differ is stated in their own sections: the
Cartesian metric has no geometric sources (@sec-ch03-cartesian), the spherical-polar metric carries curvature
sources (@sec-ch03-sphpolar), and the cubed sphere has non-orthogonal panel frames (@sec-ch03-gnomonic).

| scheme | switch | default | order | main test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| global grid, sliced per block (@sec-ch03-globalgrid) | YAML[^rg-a13a7908fab9] `geometry`[^rg-acca5c2fc359], `distribute`[^rg-6bfdf84625d7] | on | exact | `test_coordinate` |
| Cartesian metric (@sec-ch03-cartesian) | `type: cartesian` | default type | exact | `test_coordinate` |
| spherical-polar metric (@sec-ch03-sphpolar) | `type: spherical-polar` | off | exact metric | `test_coordinate` |
| gnomonic cubed sphere (@sec-ch03-gnomonic) | `type: gnomonic-equiangle` | off | exact metric | `test_cubed_sphere_cell_volume_python` |
| radial face moments (@sec-ch03-facemoments) | `SNAP_FLUX_COVARIANCE` | on | exact | `test_radial_face_moments` |
| layouts and rank maps (@sec-ch03-layouts) | `distribute: layout` | `slab` | n/a | `test_exchange_decomp` |
| physical and internal faces (@sec-ch03-physfaces) | `boundary-condition`[^rg-b3b0eed8c75a] | `reflecting` | n/a | `test_exchange_decomp` |
| generic ghost exchange (@sec-ch03-exchange) | `SyncOptions` | conserved, no corners | exact copy | `test_mesh_exchange_python` |
| cross-panel ghost interpolation (@sec-ch03-csinterp) | `interpolate` | on per stage | 2 | `test_cubed_sphere_exchange` |
| face-state seam sync (@sec-ch03-cslrsync) | none | on (cubed sphere) | exact copy | `test_flux_covariance_seams_python` |
| donor factor raw copy (@sec-ch03-thetacopy) | `limiter`[^rg-456ae36987ad] | on with the limiter or face-flux covariance (default on), with species | exact copy | `test_flux_positivity_cubedsphere_python` |
| $x_1$ seams between blocks (@sec-ch03-x1seams) | `layout: cubed`, `nb1`[^rg-09ddf5c365cf] | `nb1: 1` | round-off | `test_x1_seam_split` |
| conserved vs primitive sync (@sec-ch03-synctype) | `type`[^rg-cabddec24922] | conserved | exact | `test_coordinate` |
| $x_1$-wall corner refresh (@sec-ch03-cornerrefresh) | none | on | exact | `test_wb_wall_corner`, `test_cubed_sphere_exchange` |
| `cylindrical` stub (@sec-ch03-cylindrical) | `type: cylindrical` | off | none | none |

: The schemes of this chapter. "order" is the accuracy of the quantity the scheme produces; "exact" means equal to
the defining integral or copy up to round-off. Test names omit the `.release` suffix of C++ entries.

<!-- reader glossary notes -->
[^rg-65581851d3d4]: $x_1, x_2, x_3$ — the three coordinate directions; $x_1$ is always the vertical (radial) direction

[^rg-a13a7908fab9]: YAML — YAML Ain't Markup Language, the structured input format used for decks

[^rg-acca5c2fc359]: geometry — coordinate-system and grid options

[^rg-6bfdf84625d7]: distribute — domain-distribution options

[^rg-b3b0eed8c75a]: boundary-condition — boundary options: `external` boundary-function names for the domain faces and `internal` solid-cell settings

[^rg-456ae36987ad]: limiter — whether the enclosing component enables its limiter

[^rg-09ddf5c365cf]: nb1 — number of blocks along the first coordinate direction

[^rg-cabddec24922]: type — `SyncOptions` field choosing which variables a ghost exchange syncs (default conserved)
<!-- end reader glossary notes -->
